neighbours.label: the echoed word in the second half of a parallel saying or correlative ('great power brings great responsibility', 'the more..., the more ...')
fire: As my grandmother used to say, small kindness brings small joys every day.
Coaches often remind players that big risks bring big rewards in the final.
Everyone knows that the more people use the road, the more they expect it to be repaired.
In politics, the faction that controls the party also controls the purse.
Old sailors claimed that a red sky brings red seas by the evening.
The idea is simple: the more readers trust the paper, the more they rely on it.
As the proverb goes, hard work brings hard-won success to those who wait.
In this market, as costs rise, so do the prices of almost everything.
quiet: As my grandmother used to say, a kind word can brighten anyone's day.
Coaches often remind players that taking chances wins finals.
Everyone knows that heavy traffic wears the road down and it needs repair.
In politics, the faction that controls the party usually wins the election.
Old sailors claimed that a red sky in the morning meant a storm later.
The idea is simple: readers who trust the paper buy it every day.
As the proverb goes, patience is rewarded for those who wait.
In this market, costs are rising and buyers are worried about everything.

notes: Card: no single token; peaks on ' it' in 'the more people rely on the Internet the more people rely on it', ' comes', ' so do', ' also holds'. Probe: the peak sat on the repeated second word. 'Great power brings great responsibility' 1.18 (second ' great'), 'With great power comes great' 0.64, 'the more people depend..., the more they expect' 0.52, 'so do wages' 0.35, 'also controls' 0.30. 'The harder..., the more' 0.04 (no echo); plain paraphrases <=0.01. Label: the mirrored element of a parallel structure. Near misses keep each saying's topic without the echo.
